info.title: SpeechNexus internal asset inspection API
info.description:
Private single-request audio inspection protocol between the Speech API and
the isolated `asset-inspector` deployment unit. The inspector decodes one
untrusted encoded audio body and returns only media counts and digests; it
never reads object storage, writes PostgreSQL, publishes an Asset, or
produces a `ready` fact. The API revalidates the receipt against its own
buffered digest, byte count, media type, sample clock, and duration budget
before any durable write.

Each request carries exactly one complete body. There is no session, job
identity, idempotency key, filename, client MIME type, workspace, purpose,
or object key on this protocol. The request body is the raw encoded audio,
not JSON or base64. `200` reuses the canonical `AudioInspectionSuccess`
schema from `audio-inspection.schema.json`; this document adds no receipt
fields and keeps no semantic copy of that structure.

Unavailability and content rejection are distinct stable outcomes. A
`415 unsupported_media` / `422 invalid_media` / `422 media_limit_exceeded` is
a permanent rejection of the supplied bytes: the public upload path bounds
only the byte count, so a media type the recipe does not accept is the
caller's file, not this deployment's fault. A `429 busy`, `503 unavailable`,
or `504 deadline_exceeded` is a temporary infrastructure outcome for which a
new request may later succeed. Neither category authorizes the caller to
create an Asset row, publish an object, or infer a public `ready` state.

post.summary: Decode one complete untrusted audio upload and return media facts
post.description:
The body must be a single `audio/wav` encoding accepted by the fixed
`pcm-decode-1` recipe. The inspector validates length before decoding,
caps concurrency at its configured slot count, and never queues. A
request either receives one complete receipt or one failure envelope.

`X-Nexus-Deadline-Ms` and `X-Nexus-Max-Duration-Ms` are budget requests,
not permissions: the inspector clamps each value to its own configured
hard limit and never accepts a client-selected command, path, endpoint,
environment value, or decoder option. `X-Request-Id` is correlation-only
and must not contain content.

A body that has not been fully read with the declared `Content-Length`
does not start decoding. The inspector recomputes the digest and byte
count over the bytes it actually received; the API compares them with
its own values, so transport substitution or request mixing is
detectable.

requestBody.description:
Raw encoded audio bytes. `Content-Type` is exactly
`application/octet-stream`; JSON wrappers and base64 are not accepted.
The body is capped by the smaller of the API asset byte limit and the
inspector encoded-byte limit. The API rejects a body over its own
limit before making this request, so `413` here indicates a deployment
configuration mismatch rather than a content rejection.

200.description:
Complete decode receipt. The body is exactly `AudioInspectionSuccess`
from `audio-inspection.schema.json`; the API rejects an unknown field,
a non-`audio/wav` media type, a digest or byte mismatch, an implausible
sample clock, a duration over its configured limit, or a receipt over
its configured response-byte bound. A receipt that fails revalidation
is API-side unavailability, never content rejection.

X-Request-ID.description: Correlation ID echoed from the request when supplied.

422.description:
One of two permanent content outcomes. `invalid_media` means the
complete body is not an acceptable WAV (truncated, inconsistent RIFF,
malformed chunk structure, or non-PCM). `media_limit_exceeded` means
the media itself exceeds the duration or decode budget while the
inspector wall clock had not expired. The API maps `invalid_media`
to public `422 invalid_asset_audio` and `media_limit_exceeded` to
public `422 asset_audio_too_long`; neither writes an Asset row,
object, or event.

ContentLengthHeader.name: Content-Length
ContentLengthHeader.description:
Exact encoded body length in bytes. Missing, non-numeric, or a value that
does not equal the bytes actually received is `400 bad_request`; the
inspector does not start decoding a short or over-declared body.

DeadlineBudgetHeader.name: X-Nexus-Deadline-Ms
DeadlineBudgetHeader.description:
Wall-clock decode budget in milliseconds for this request. It covers
decoding only and is clamped to the inspector's configured maximum. On
expiry the inspector kills the decoder child process and returns
`504 deadline_exceeded`.

MaxDurationHeader.name: X-Nexus-Max-Duration-Ms
MaxDurationHeader.description:
Media duration ceiling in milliseconds for this request. It is a budget
request clamped to the inspector's configured maximum. A media duration
over the effective ceiling is `422 media_limit_exceeded` while the wall
clock is still valid.

XRequestIdHeader.name: X-Request-ID
XRequestIdHeader.description:
Opaque client correlation value. It must not contain audio, filenames,
paths, credentials, or business content, and it does not select an
endpoint or change decode behavior.

AssetInspectionFailure.description:
Closed private failure envelope. It carries no vendor message, command,
path, token, input fragment, or stack trace. The stable `status` value is
the only discriminator; consumers must not parse prose.

BadRequest.description:
`Content-Length` is missing or disagrees with the received byte count, or
another request header is malformed. The body is not decoded and no
receipt is produced. The API treats this as internal protocol violation
and maps it to public `503 asset_inspection_unavailable`, never to a
content rejection.

Unauthorized.description:
The bearer token is missing or wrong. This is a deployment configuration
failure, not a caller input problem; the API maps it to public
`503 asset_inspection_unavailable`. The response never echoes the token.

EncodedTooLarge.description:
The encoded body exceeds the inspector byte cap. This is a deployment
limit mismatch, not a permanent content verdict; the API maps it to
public `503 asset_inspection_unavailable`.

UnsupportedMedia.description:
The media type is not one this recipe accepts. The public upload path
bounds the byte count but never filters the media type, so the file
reaches the inspector exactly as the caller supplied it: an unsupported
encoding is a permanent content verdict, not an outage, and a new
request with the same bytes cannot succeed. The API maps this to public
`422 invalid_asset_audio`, the same code as `invalid_media`. No Asset
row, object, event, or Job is written.

Busy.description:
Every configured inspection slot is in use. The inspector has no queue:
it rejects immediately instead of holding the connection. A new request
later may succeed, and a repeated inspection of the same bytes has no
side effects. The API maps this to public `503 asset_inspection_busy`
with `retryable: true`.

Unavailable.description:
The inspector is not ready, its startup self-check failed, or a decoder
child process failed unexpectedly. A new request may succeed after the
deployment unit restarts, but this response proves no content verdict and
writes no state. The API maps this to public
`503 asset_inspection_busy`: the inspector is configured, but this
request cannot be served now.

DeadlineExceeded.description:
The clamped wall-clock deadline expired and the inspector killed the
decoder child process. This is a temporary budget outcome, not evidence
that the media is invalid; the API maps it to public
`503 asset_inspection_busy` with `retryable: true`. The slot is released
only after the child is dead.

InspectionBearer.description:
Deployment-injected token accepted only by the inspector. It is separate
from the public shared service key and from every component credential
used by the execution gateway or node controller. The inspector compares
it in constant time; a missing or wrong token returns `401`. The token
never appears in a response, log, or error message.
